stem: Let $X=\{{=xs}\}$ and $Y=\{{=ys}\}$. The cartesian product $X\times Y$ is represented by an arrow diagram, in which each ordered pair is an arrow from its first projection (an element of $X$) to its second projection (an element of $Y$). How many arrows are drawn in the diagram?
solution: The set $X$ has {=m} elements and $Y$ has {=n} elements.
Each ordered pair of $X\times Y$ is one arrow, from an element of $X$ to an element of $Y$.
Each of the {=m} elements of $X$ has an arrow to each of the {=n} elements of $Y$.
notes: Basic: count arrows of arrow diagram; builds on book example 4.
